    uncertain.

    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",

# Outcome sub-dossier — Parkway, Inc. realized record after going-private merger, ~3-5-year horizon (~2020-2022)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the entity was taken private and
> deregistered, there is no post-closing public 10-K; the traceable realized record is
> limited to the deregistration filing and company disclosures. This sub-dossier
> contains no information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- On October 23, 2017, Parkway, Inc. filed a Form 15-12B certifying termination of
  registration of its common stock under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act and
  suspension of its duty to file reports under Sections 13(a)/15(d); the filing recorded
  approximately 1 holder of record as of the certification date. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-17-316665, Form 15-12B]
- A search of Parkway, Inc.'s (CIK 0001677761) EDGAR filing history for annual reports
  finds no Form 10-K or Form 20-F filed after the pre-merger FY2016 10-K (filed
  2017-03-15); no periodic report covering fiscal years within the ~2020-2022 outcome
  window was located. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001677761&type=10-K]
- No public audited financial statements are available for the acquired Houston office
  portfolio for the ~2020-2022 window; CPPIB is a large diversified pension investment
  manager and no source was found in which it separately discloses this specific
  acquired business's post-close trajectory. [UNVERIFIED]

## Realized record of the separated management entity (company disclosure, imprecisely dated)
- The current company website of Parkway Property Investments — a firm formed by former
  Parkway executives at the time of the CPPIB transaction — states that, "Following the
  CPPIB merger, [James] Heistand acquires Parkway's management platform and establishes
  Parkway Property Investments as a privately held firm with institutional-grade
  standards," and that the firm went on to "build its office portfolio across key
  Sunbelt markets in partnership with leading investors and expand into industrial and
  multifamily development." [SRC: https://www.pky.com/our-story]
- The same source states that "In 2023, Parkway closed a 3M square foot acquisition in
  Houston, marking one of the largest U.S. real estate transactions of the year." [SRC: https://www.pky.com/our-story]
- The source does not state whether this management entity continued to manage the
  specific Houston office portfolio acquired by CPPIB in 2017, nor does it give a
  precise date (within vs. outside the ~2020-2022 window) for when its independent
  portfolio activity began. [UNVERIFIED]

## Items sought but not found
- No reputable-press or primary source was located reporting a divestiture, impairment,
  write-down, bankruptcy, or comparable outcome scalar specifically tied to the
  CPPIB-owned former-Parkway Houston office portfolio within the ~2020-2022 window.
  General industry reporting on Houston office-market vacancy and on CPPIB's
  portfolio-wide reduction of office real estate exposure exists but does not name this
  specific former-Parkway asset base or attribute a scalar to it, so it is not cited
  here as an outcome fact for this case. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because Parkway, Inc. was taken private and deregistered in October 2017, there is no
  public audited outcome record (10-K/20-F) for the ~2020-2022 window for the acquired
  Houston office business itself. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-17-316665, Form 15-12B]
- The only traceable post-close realized-record fact concerns the separated management
  entity, which the company's own current website states became an independent privately
  held real estate firm that subsequently pursued acquisitions in other Sunbelt markets;
  no source was found isolating the trajectory of the acquired Houston office portfolio
  itself within the fixed outcome window. [SRC: https://www.pky.com/our-story]
- Per the no-record convention, this case is coded **uncertain** on the outcome for the
  acquired business: the absence of a public periodic-reporting record precludes a
  sourced determination of the realized 3-5-year trajectory of the specific acquired
  asset base.

[SLICE END]
